Medical laboratory scientist jobs and[medical technologist vacancies](https://www.amnhealthcare.com/jobs/c/Allied/?filters=Discipline:Medical+Technologist/Clinical+Lab+Scientist) are in high demand across the U.S., driven by a nationwide shortage of lab professionals. Hospitals, reference laboratories, and point-of-care settings are actively hiring. AMN Healthcare connects qualified candidates with open medical laboratory scientist MLS jobs nationwide.


Laboratory professionals are the backbone of modern medicine. Behind every diagnosis, treatment decision, and patient outcome is a medical laboratory scientist or medical technologist analyzing specimens, running quality checks, and delivering results that clinicians depend on. And right now, healthcare facilities across the country need more of them.


If you hold a degree and certification in medical laboratory science, the job market is working in your favor.


## Why Are Medical Technologist Vacancies at an All-Time High?


The lab workforce is shrinking. A significant portion of experienced medical laboratory scientists are approaching retirement age, and the pipeline of new graduates has not kept pace with demand. At the same time, testing volumes have climbed steadily across hospitals, diagnostic labs, and specialty centers.


The result: healthcare facilities are competing for a limited pool of qualified professionals, which has pushed[salaries](https://www.amnhealthcare.com/careers/allied/resources/allied-pay/) up and created openings across a wide range of settings and regions.


## What Types of Medical Laboratory Scientist Jobs Are Available?


Medical laboratory scientist[MLS](https://www.amnhealthcare.com/careers/allied/medical-laboratory/) jobs span a broad range of settings, each with its own pace, patient population, and specialty focus.


- **Hospital laboratories** offer exposure to diverse testing disciplines, including hematology, microbiology, chemistry, and blood banking. These roles tend to offer variety and strong benefits packages.
- **Reference laboratories** handle high-volume, specialized testing. These environments suit professionals who thrive on consistency and technical precision at scale.
- **Point-of-care settings** , such as clinics and urgent care centers, offer smaller, faster-paced environments where lab professionals work closely with clinical teams.
- **Travel laboratory assignments** provide geographic flexibility and typically come with higher pay, housing stipends, and the chance to build experience across multiple settings.


## What Skills Do Employers Look for in Medical Technologist Jobs?


Employers filling medical technologist vacancies look for a consistent set of competencies, regardless of setting:


- **Technical proficiency** with laboratory instrumentation and quality assurance protocols
- **Attention to detail** and a commitment to accuracy in all diagnostic work
- **Efficiency under pressure** , particularly in high-volume or time-sensitive environments
- **Clear communication skills** for coordinating with physicians, nurses, and interdisciplinary care teams


Certifications from the American Society for Clinical Pathology (ASCP) or the American Medical Technologists (AMT) organization remain the standard credential employers expect. Staying current with continuing education requirements also strengthens your candidacy.


## How to Land a Medical Laboratory Scientist Job


### How should I structure my resume for medical laboratory scientist MLS jobs?


Lead with your certifications and licensure, then highlight any specialized instrumentation experience or testing disciplines where you have deep knowledge. Quantify your contributions where possible, volume of
specimens processed, accuracy rates, or quality improvement initiatives you contributed to.


### Should I consider travel medical technologist jobs?


Travel assignments are worth serious consideration if you want to accelerate your earnings, gain experience in different lab environments, or explore new regions of the country. Many travel lab professionals earn significantly more than their permanent counterparts when factoring in stipends and assignment bonuses.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What certifications do I need for medical laboratory scientist jobs?


Most employers require ASCP or AMT certification. Some states also require licensure. Specific requirements vary by state and employer.


### Are travel medical technologist vacancies paid more than permanent roles?


Travel medical technologist jobs typically offer higher base pay, plus housing stipends and travel reimbursements, making total compensation higher than many permanent positions.
